# Complexity

Every Zazr collection states the cost of its methods in their javadoc. This page gathers those notes, so it always matches the code.

## How to read a cost

A cost is the worst case of one call, in big-O notation, unless its note says otherwise. The letters mean:

- n: the number of elements of the collection you call the method on.
- m: the number of elements of the argument.
- k: a count the note names, such as the elements taken or dropped.
- i and j: index arguments; a slice runs from i to j.
- size and step: the window size and the step of `sliding` and `grouped`.

In the tables, hover a cost to read its whole note.

## Classes of cost

Each cost falls in one of these classes, cheapest first. The Scala column gives the abbreviation of the same class in Scala's collections documentation, for readers who know it.

## Effectively constant

`Vector`, `HashSet` and `HashMap` keep their elements in wide, shallow trees of small arrays, 32 slots each. A lookup reads one array per level: four levels hold a million elements, seven hold the largest possible collection. An update copies those few arrays and shares the rest.

This is a worst case, not an average: every call costs a handful of steps.

## Amortised constant

An amortised cost is an average. Most calls are O(1), and now and then one call pays O(n) for the work the others skipped.

The average holds over a chain of calls, each made on the result of the previous one. A Zazr collection never changes, so you can also call the method again on an older version: each such call may pay the O(n) step again. The note of each amortised method says when that happens.

## Lazy

A `Stream` computes its elements when they are read, and keeps each one once computed. A lazy call returns a `Stream` without walking this one: its note says what is computed now, and the rest is computed as you read the result.

"Now" can still be more than one element. A call that keeps only some elements, such as `filter`, reads until its first kept element; on an infinite `Stream` where none is kept, it never returns.

## Missing operations

`n/a` in a table means that the type has no such method. `HashSet` and `HashMap` have no positional methods (`head`, `take`, `drop`), because their order is not defined.

## Sequences

`NonEmptyVector` wraps a `Vector`, so its costs are those of `Vector`. `Stream` is lazy: most of its operations compute their result as it is read.

## Sets

`head`, `take` and `drop` exist only where the order is defined: insertion order on `LinkedHashSet`, the comparator's order on `TreeSet`.

The removed element makes a gap in the insertion order, and the whole set is rebuilt in O(n) once the gaps outnumber the elements; removing the first or the last element also walks past the gaps next to it. Over a chain of removals, each on the result of the previous one, this averages to effectively O(1); removing again from an older version can pay O(n) every time.">amortised O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): one deletion from the tree.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `union` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for a set of m elements, each an effectively O(1) insertion; this set, or a HashSet argument, is returned as is when the other side is empty.">O(m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for a set of m elements, each an effectively O(1) add; this set, or a LinkedHashSet argument, is returned as is when the other side is empty.">O(m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(m log(n + m)) for a set of m elements: one lookup each, then one insertion for each new one. When elements is a TreeSet with an equal comparator (for a lambda, the same object), the cost is O(m log(n / m + 1)), m then being the smaller of the two sizes: the two trees are cut and joined, not rebuilt.">O(m log(n + m))</abbr> |
| `intersect` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for a set of m elements; O(min(n, m)) when it is a HashSet: the elements of the smaller set are checked against the larger one. Another kind of set is first copied into a hash set.">O(m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for a set of m elements; O(n) when it is a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it and the kept ones are put in a new set.">O(n + m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(m + n log n) for a set of m elements: they are put in a hash set, then the kept elements are inserted one by one into a new tree. When elements is a TreeSet with an equal comparator (for a lambda, the same object), the cost is O(m log(n / m + 1)), m then being the smaller of the two sizes: the two trees are cut and joined, not rebuilt.">O(m + n log n)</abbr> |
| `diff` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for a set of m elements; O(n) when it is a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it: the whole set is walked even to remove one element, which remove does in effectively O(1).">O(n + m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for a set of m elements; O(n) when it is a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it and the kept ones are put in a new set: the whole set is walked even to remove one element, which remove does in amortised O(1).">O(n + m)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(m + n log n) for a set of m elements: they are put in a hash set, then the kept elements are inserted one by one into a new tree. When elements is a TreeSet with an equal comparator (for a lambda, the same object), the cost is O(m log(n / m + 1)), m then being the smaller of the two sizes: the two trees are cut and joined, not rebuilt.">O(m + n log n)</abbr> |
| `min` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, head() gives the least element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, head() gives the least element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, head() gives the least element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> |
| `max` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, last() gives the greatest element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, last() gives the greatest element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, last() gives the greatest element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> |
| `head` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): the first element of the insertion order.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the smallest element is found by walking down the tree, with no comparison.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `take` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n); O(min(k, n - k)) for k kept elements when nothing has been removed: the smaller side, kept or dropped, is added to or taken out of a hash map, and the rest is shared. After removals, finding the cut walks past the gaps left by removed elements, and the result is rebuilt when it holds more gaps than elements.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the tree is cut at that position without visiting the elements, and the result shares the rest of the tree.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `drop` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n); O(min(k, n - k)) for k dropped elements on a set with no earlier removals, as take.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the tree is cut at that position without visiting the elements, and the result shares the rest of the tree.">O(log n)</abbr> |

## Maps

As for the sets, only the ordered maps have positional methods.

| Operation | `HashMap` | `LinkedHashMap` | `TreeMap` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): one walk down the tree, comparing keys with the comparator.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `containsKey` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): one walk down the tree, comparing keys with the comparator.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `put` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup and one put.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup and one put.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): one lookup, then one insertion.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `remove` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this map.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-amortisedconstant" title="amortised O(1); a single call can cost O(n). The removed entry makes a gap in the insertion order, and the whole map is rebuilt in O(n) once the gaps outnumber the entries; removing the first or the last entry also walks past the gaps next to it. Over a chain of removals, each on the result of the previous one, this averages to effectively O(1); removing again from an older version can pay O(n) every time.">amortised O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): one lookup, then one deletion when the key is present.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `keySet` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): the keys are copied into a new HashSet.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): a LinkedHashSet view that shares this map; nothing is copied.">O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(n log n): the keys are inserted one by one into a new TreeSet.">O(n log n)</abbr> |
| `values` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): the values are copied into a new Vector.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): the values are copied into a new Vector.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): one walk in key order, the values copied into a Vector.">O(n)</abbr> |
| `head` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): the first key of the insertion order, then one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the entry with the smallest key is found by walking down the tree, with no comparison.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `take` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n); O(min(k, n - k)) for k kept entries when nothing has been removed: the smaller side, kept or dropped, is added to or taken out of a hash map, and the rest is shared. After removals, finding the cut walks past the gaps left by removed entries, and the result is rebuilt when it holds more gaps than entries.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the tree is cut at that position without visiting the entries, and the result shares the rest of the tree.">O(log n)</abbr> |
| `drop` | n/a | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n); O(min(k, n - k)) for k dropped entries on a map with no earlier removals, as take.">O(n)</abbr> | <abbr class="cx cx-logarithmic" title="O(log n): the tree is cut at that position without visiting the entries, and the result shares the rest of the tree.">O(log n)</abbr> |

## Every method, per type

Each type lists its methods that have a cost note, in the order of its source. A method inherited from an interface says so. The paragraph under each type covers its other methods.

### `Vector`

The methods without a note of their own (map, filter, flatMap, the folds, groupBy, the conversions, and the factories such as ofAll and range) walk the elements once: O(n), where n is the size of the result for a factory and flatMap. containsAll is O(n * m): one contains per element of its argument.

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `transpose(Vector<Vector<T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-polynomial" title="O(rows * columns); the matrix itself is returned when it has no or one element.">O(rows * columns)</abbr> | O(rows * columns); the matrix itself is returned when it has no or one element. |
| `flatten(Iterable<? extends Iterable<? extends T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m inner elements in total, each added to the result once.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m inner elements in total, each added to the result once. |
| `append(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): copies a few small arrays of 32 elements, not the Vector. On a Vector of primitive values, a value of another class first converts every element: O(n), paid again at each such write on the same Vector (see the class documentation).">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): copies a few small arrays of 32 elements, not the Vector. On a Vector of primitive values, a value of another class first converts every element: O(n), paid again at each such write on the same Vector (see the class documentation). |
| `appendAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m appended elements, even when this Vector is much shorter than the argument; the elements of this Vector are shared, not copied. O(1) when this Vector is empty and iterable is a Vector, which is returned as is. On a Vector of primitive values, a value of another class first converts every element: O(n), paid again at each such write on the same Vector (see the class documentation).">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m appended elements, even when this Vector is much shorter than the argument; the elements of this Vector are shared, not copied. O(1) when this Vector is empty and iterable is a Vector, which is returned as is. On a Vector of primitive values, a value of another class first converts every element: O(n), paid again at each such write on the same Vector (see the class documentation). |
| `asJava()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. get on the view is effectively O(1), as get, and each step of its iterator is O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. get on the view is effectively O(1), as get, and each step of its iterator is O(1). |
| `combinations()` | <abbr class="cx cx-combinatorial" title="O(n * 2^n): the 2^n combinations hold n * 2^(n - 1) elements in all, and building them visits as many partial choices.">O(n * 2^n)</abbr> | O(n * 2^n): the 2^n combinations hold n * 2^(n - 1) elements in all, and building them visits as many partial choices. |
| `combinations(int)` | <abbr class="cx cx-combinatorial" title="O(k * C(n, k) + C(n, 0) + ... + C(n, k)): the C(n, k) combinations of k elements are built, and every choice of fewer than k elements is visited on the way, even one that cannot be completed. ### `List`

The methods without a note of their own (map, flatMap, the folds, groupBy, the conversions, equals, hashCode, toString) walk the elements once: O(n); an Option variant costs what the method it wraps costs, and toStream() is O(1), its elements being read as the Stream reaches them. A List does not store its size, so equals, toArray(), stream() and spliterator() count the elements before they start, and containsAll is O(n * m) for m elements: each one is looked for by a walk.

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `isEmpty()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1). |
| `flatten(Iterable<? extends Iterable<? extends T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m inner elements in total: each is copied once, and the result is reversed once.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m inner elements in total: each is copied once, and the result is reversed once. |
| `transpose(List<List<T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-polynomial" title="O(rows * columns): every element is copied once.">O(rows * columns)</abbr> | O(rows * columns): every element is copied once. |
| `append(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n); every element of this List is copied.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n); every element of this List is copied. |
| `appendAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for m appended elements; this List and the appended elements are copied.">O(n + m)</abbr> | O(n + m) for m appended elements; this List and the appended elements are copied. |
| `asJava()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. On the view, get(i) is O(i), so a loop by index is O(n^2): iterate the view instead. size() is O(n) the first time, then O(1): the view keeps it.">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. ### `Queue`

A Queue keeps its last elements in reverse order (those added at its back since it last put them in order, or those init moved there), and puts them in order in one O(n) step when a call needs them; the notes call them &quot;the elements held at the back&quot;. The methods without a note of their own (map, flatMap, partition, the folds, the conversions, the static factories) walk the elements once: O(n); toSortedSet and toSortedMap sort them, O(n log n); toQueue, and ofAll given a Queue, are O(1).

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `flatten(Iterable<? extends Iterable<? extends T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n) for n inner elements in total.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n) for n inner elements in total. |
| `transpose(Queue<Queue<T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-polynomial" title="O(rows * columns).">O(rows * columns)</abbr> | O(rows * columns). |
| `enqueue(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1). |
| `enqueueAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m enqueued elements.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m enqueued elements. |
| `containsSlice(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-polynomial" title="O(n * m) for a slice of m elements.">O(n * m)</abbr> | O(n * m) for a slice of m elements. |

### `NonEmptyVector`

Every method costs what the same method of the wrapped Vector costs; wrapping and unwrapping copy nothing. The methods without a note of their own (map, flatMap, filter, the folds, groupBy, the conversions and the factories) walk the elements once: O(n).

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `transpose(NonEmptyVector<? extends NonEmptyVector<? extends A>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-polynomial" title="O(rows * columns), as Vector.transpose.">O(rows * columns)</abbr> | O(rows * columns), as Vector.transpose. |
| `append(A)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1), as Vector.append, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1), as Vector.append, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `appendAll(Vector<? extends A>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m appended elements, as Vector.appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m appended elements, as Vector.appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `appendAll(NonEmptyVector<? extends A>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m appended elements, as Vector.appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m appended elements, as Vector.appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `concat(NonEmptyVector<? extends A>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m appended elements, as appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m appended elements, as appendAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `prepend(A)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1), as Vector.prepend, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1), as Vector.prepend, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `prependAll(Vector<? extends A>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m prepended elements, as Vector.prependAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m prepended elements, as Vector.prependAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |
| `prependAll(NonEmptyVector<? extends A>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m prepended elements, as Vector.prependAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m prepended elements, as Vector.prependAll, including its O(n) case on primitive values. |

### `HashSet`

Lookups, insertions and removals are effectively O(1); an insertion or a removal copies a few small arrays and shares the rest with the original set. The methods without a note of their own (map, filter, the folds, the conversions) walk the elements once, O(n), and those that build a new set insert each kept element in effectively O(1).

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `flatten(Iterable<? extends Iterable<? extends T>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m inner elements in total, one effectively O(1) insertion each.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m inner elements in total, one effectively O(1) insertion each. |
| `add(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup; a new element also costs a copy of a few small arrays, the rest is shared with this set.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup; a new element also costs a copy of a few small arrays, the rest is shared with this set. |
| `addAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for m elements, each an effectively O(1) insertion; O(1) when this set is empty and elements is a HashSet, which is returned as is.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for m elements, each an effectively O(1) insertion; O(1) when this set is empty and elements is a HashSet, which is returned as is. |
| `contains(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `diff(Set<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for a set of m elements; O(n) when it is a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it: the whole set is walked even to remove one element, which remove does in effectively O(1).">O(n + m)</abbr> | O(n + m) for a set of m elements; O(n) when it is a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it: the whole set is walked even to remove one element, which remove does in effectively O(1). |
| `intersect(Set<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for a set of m elements; O(min(n, m)) when it is a HashSet: the elements of the smaller set are checked against the larger one. Another kind of set is first copied into a hash set.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for a set of m elements; O(min(n, m)) when it is a HashSet: the elements of the smaller set are checked against the larger one. Another kind of set is first copied into a hash set. |
| `isEmpty()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1). |
| `size()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): the size is stored, not counted.">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): the size is stored, not counted. |
| `iterator()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n). |
| `asJava()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. contains on the view is effectively O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. contains on the view is effectively O(1). |
| `partitionMap(Function<? super T, ? extends Either<? extends L, ? extends R>>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): one effectively O(1) insertion per element.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): one effectively O(1) insertion per element. |
| `remove(T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this set.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this set. |
| `removeAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for m given elements; O(n) when they are a HashSet. | `replace(T, T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup, one removal and one insertion.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup, one removal and one insertion. |
| `replaceAll(T, T)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1), as replace: a set holds an element once.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1), as replace: a set holds an element once. |
| `retainAll(Iterable<? extends T>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n + m) for m given elements; O(n) when they are a HashSet. The m elements are put in a hash set (unless they already are one), then every element of this set is checked against it.">O(n + m)</abbr> | O(n + m) for m given elements; O(n) when they are a HashSet. O(1) when the sizes differ.">O(n log n)</abbr> | O(n log n) against a TreeSet, O(n) against a HashSet or a LinkedHashSet: after a size check, each element of this set is looked up in the other one. | `hashCode()` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): computed from every element on each call; it is not cached.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): computed from every element on each call; it is not cached. |
| `max()` (from `Set`) | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, last() gives the greatest element in the set's own order in O(log n).">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): every element is compared in its natural order. On a TreeSet, last() gives the greatest element in the set's own order in O(log n). |

### `LinkedHashSet`

It is a LinkedHashMap of its elements and has the same costs. Lookups and insertions are effectively O(1). Removing an element makes a gap in the insertion order, and the whole set is rebuilt in O(n) once the gaps outnumber the elements: averaged over a chain of removals, each on the result of the previous one, a removal is effectively O(1), but removing again from an older version can pay the O(n) every time, and after removals, finding a position (tail, take, drop) walks past the gaps in the way. The methods without a note of their own (map, filter, the folds, the conversions) walk the elements once, O(n).

### `TreeSet`

The methods without a note of their own are O(n) at most, one walk over the elements (the folds, find, count, tap, hashCode, toString, toList), except size, isEmpty and comparator, O(1), and containsAll, one lookup per element, O(m log n). toSortedMap and toSortedSet(Comparator) insert the elements one by one into a new tree: O(n log n). The factories (of, ofAll, range, tabulate, fill, collector) insert the elements one by one: O(m log m) for m elements, even when they come sorted.

O(1) when values is a TreeSet created without a comparator, or its asJava view: that set is returned as is.">O(m log m)</abbr> | O(m log m) for m elements: each one is inserted into the tree, even when they come sorted. O(1) when values is a TreeSet created without a comparator, or its asJava view: that set is returned as is. |

### `HashMap`

Lookups, insertions and removals by key are effectively O(1); an insertion or a removal copies a few small arrays and shares the rest with the original map. The methods without a note of their own (map, filter, the folds, the conversions) walk the entries once, O(n), and those that build a new map insert each kept entry in effectively O(1).

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `computeIfAbsent(K, Function<? super K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is absent.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is absent. |
| `computeIfPresent(K, BiFunction<? super K, ? super V, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is present.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is present. |
| `contains(Tuple2<K, V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup of the key, then its value is compared.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup of the key, then its value is compared. |
| `containsKey(K)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `get(K)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `getOrElse(K, V)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `isEmpty()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1). |
| `iterator()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n). |
| `keySet()` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): the keys are copied into a new HashSet.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): the keys are copied into a new HashSet. |
| `merge(Map<? extends K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(m) for a map of m entries, one lookup and at most one put each; O(1) when that map is empty, or when this map is empty and that map is a HashMap, which is returned as is.">O(m)</abbr> | O(m) for a map of m entries, one lookup and at most one put each; O(1) when that map is empty, or when this map is empty and that map is a HashMap, which is returned as is. |

| `put(K, V)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this map.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this map. |
| `put(Tuple2<? extends K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1), as put.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1), as put. |

| `remove(K)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this map.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup, then a copy of a few small arrays; the rest is shared with this map. |

| `size()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): the size is stored, not counted.">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): the size is stored, not counted. |
| `asJavaMap()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. get and containsKey on the view are effectively O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. get and containsKey on the view are effectively O(1). |
| `values()` | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): the values are copied into a new Vector.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): the values are copied into a new Vector. |
| `equals(Object)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(n log n) against a TreeMap, O(n) against a HashMap or a LinkedHashMap: after a size check, each entry of this map is looked up in the other one. | `min()` (from `Map`) | <abbr class="cx cx-linear" title="O(n): every entry is compared in the natural order of its key, then of its value.">O(n)</abbr> | O(n): every entry is compared in the natural order of its key, then of its value. |
| `asJava()` (from `Traversable`) | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. On the view, contains costs what this collection's own contains costs.">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. On the view, contains costs what this collection's own contains costs. |

### `LinkedHashMap`

Lookups and insertions are effectively O(1). Removing an entry makes a gap in the insertion order, and the whole map is rebuilt in O(n) once the gaps outnumber the entries: averaged over a chain of removals, each on the result of the previous one, a removal is effectively O(1), but removing again from an older version can pay the O(n) every time, and after removals, finding a position (tail, take, drop) walks past the gaps in the way. The methods without a note of their own (map, filter, the folds, the conversions) walk the entries once, O(n).

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `computeIfAbsent(K, Function<? super K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is absent.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is absent. |
| `computeIfPresent(K, BiFunction<? super K, ? super V, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is present.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup, and one put when the key is present. |
| `contains(Tuple2<K, V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one lookup of the key, then its value is compared.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one lookup of the key, then its value is compared. |
| `containsKey(K)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `get(K)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `getOrElse(K, V)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1): one hash lookup.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1): one hash lookup. |
| `isEmpty()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1). |
| `iterator()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n). A step skips the gaps left by removed entries, so after removals a single step can take up to O(n).">O(1)</abbr> | O(1) to create; a whole walk is O(n). A step skips the gaps left by removed entries, so after removals a single step can take up to O(n). |
| `asJavaMap()` | <abbr class="cx cx-constant" title="O(1): nothing is copied. get and containsKey on the view are effectively O(1); its iterators, in either order, walk the whole map in O(n), and after removals a single step can skip many gaps.">O(1)</abbr> | O(1): nothing is copied. get and containsKey on the view are effectively O(1); its iterators, in either order, walk the whole map in O(n), and after removals a single step can skip many gaps. |

An existing key keeps its position; a new key is added at the end of the insertion order. |
| `put(Tuple2<? extends K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-effectivelyconstant" title="effectively O(1), as put.">effectively O(1)</abbr> | effectively O(1), as put. |

### `TreeMap`

The methods without a note of their own are O(n) at most, one walk over the entries (the folds, find, count, tap, hashCode, toString, toList), except size, isEmpty and comparator, O(1), and containsAll, one lookup per entry, O(m log n). toSortedMap and toSortedSet insert the entries one by one into a new tree: O(n log n). The factories (of, ofAll, ofEntries, tabulate, fill, collector) insert the entries one by one: O(m log m) for m entries, even when they come sorted.

| Method | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `ofAll(Map<? extends K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(m log m) for m entries: each one is inserted into the tree, even when they come sorted. O(1) when map is the asJavaMap view of a TreeMap created without a comparator: that map is returned as is.">O(m log m)</abbr> | O(m log m) for m entries: each one is inserted into the tree, even when they come sorted. O(1) when map is the asJavaMap view of a TreeMap created without a comparator: that map is returned as is. |
| `ofAll(Comparator<? super K>, Map<? extends K, ? extends V>)` | <abbr class="cx cx-linearithmic" title="O(m log m) for m entries: each one is inserted into the tree, even when they come sorted.
